findings: plan_select_node.cpp SubqueryToWindowRewriter: the guards are general and sufficient. It requires exactly one correlated scalar MIN/MAX (no DISTINCT/FILTER/ORDER BY) over a GET/CROSS_PRODUCT/FILTER tree. Each subquery scan must map to a distinct outer scan of the same table, with no table filters. Every remapped subquery conjunct must match an outer conjunct. Unmatched outer conjuncts may only reference the extra tables. Correlated columns must be depth 1, sit on an extra table, appear in an equality, and have a type whose partitioning is not coarser than equality (floats excluded). Volatile expressions and nested subqueries are rejected. An empty partition yields no outer rows, so MIN's NULL-on-empty result cannot be observed, and duplicate rows are harmless for MIN/MAX. No names or literals are used.

bloom_filter.cpp exact mode: only for integral keys (8/16/32-bit and int64) whose build [min, max] range is under 128 bits per build row and under 2^29 bits. NULL build keys are skipped; probe NULLs follow filters_null_values. An out-of-range insert sets an overflow flag that passes all rows, and a mismatched probe key type also passes all rows. FilterValue (used by the multi-file column mapper) handles exact mode.

join_hashtable.cpp: the exact bitmap is filled from layout column 0, which is correct because the constructor asserts that equality conditions come first (lines 49-54). That makes the mixed equality + non-equality BF safe.

row_group_collection.cpp: morsel size is derived from the configured thread count and capped at one row group. processed_rows and vector_index are updated consistently, and verify_parallelism still uses 1-vector morsels. No extra threads or memory are used.
The merge itself combines nothing: the two patches touch disjoint logic, and the author reports no regression across the two templates.
